papers.title: SimCP-NS: Similarity-based Copy Paste for Semi-Supervised 3D EM Neuron Segmentation
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Semi-supervised neuron segmentation in 3D electron microscopy (EM) is important for connectomics because it enables accurate neuron reconstruction while reducing dependence on costly manual annotations. However, existing approaches remain limited by the distribution mismatch between the small labeled dataset and the much larger unlabeled dataset, where the labeled data fails to adequately capture the true data distribution, leading models trained on them to generate low-quality segmentation masks and ultimately degrading overall performance. Results To address this issue, we propose a similarity-based copy-paste for semi-supervised 3D EM neuron segmentation (SimCP-NS) method, which employs a similarity-based copy-paste strategy to exchange the least similar labeled and unlabeled sub-volumes, thereby enriching data diversity and mitigating distribution mismatch. A teacher network is first pre-trained on unlabeled volumes to capture structural priors, which subsequently guides the student segmentation network. During student training, the similarity-based copy-paste mechanism generates hybrid samples and constructs supervision targets by fusing teacher-generated pseudo-labels with ground-truth affinity maps, optimized via mean squared error loss. Invariant representation learning is further integrated to enhance robustness of the proposed method. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of SimCP-NS over existing 3D EM neuron segmentation methods
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Semi-supervised neuron segmentation in 3D electron microscopy (EM) is important for connectomics because it enables accurate neuron reconstruction while reducing dependence on costly manual annotations. However, existing approaches remain limited by the distribution mismatch between the small labeled dataset and the much larger unlabeled dataset, where the labeled data fails to adequately capture the true data distribution, leading models trained on them to generate low-quality segmentation masks and ultimately degrading overall performance.

RESULTS: To address this issue, we propose a similarity-based copy-paste for semi-supervised 3D EM neuron segmentation (SimCP-NS) method, which employs a similarity-based copy-paste strategy to exchange the least similar labeled and unlabeled sub-volumes, thereby enriching data diversity and mitigating distribution mismatch. A teacher network is first pre-trained on unlabeled volumes to capture structural priors, which subsequently guides the student segmentation network. During student training, the similarity-based copy-paste mechanism generates hybrid samples and constructs supervision targets by fusing teacher-generated pseudo-labels with ground-truth affinity maps, optimized via mean squared error loss. Invariant representation learning is further integrated to enhance robustness of the proposed method. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of SimCP-NS over existing 3D EM neuron segmentation methods.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Codes and other supporting materials are provided in the Supplementary Material.

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：在三维电子显微镜中采用半监督方法进行神经元分割对于连接组学研究而言具有重要意义，因为这种方法能够在减少对昂贵人工注释依赖的同时，实现精确的神经元重建。
llm_highlights_zh: 然而，现有的方法仍然受到小规模标记数据集与大规模未标记数据集之间分布不匹配的限制——标记数据无法充分反映真实的数据分布情况，因此基于这些数据训练出的模型所生成的分割结果质量较差，进而导致整体性能下降。
结果：为了解决这一问题，我们提出了一种基于相似性的复制粘贴方法，用于半监督式的3D电磁神经元分割任务——即SimCP-NS方法。该方法通过利用相似性原则来替换那些标签差异最大的标记子体积与未标记子体积，从而有效提升数据多样性并缓解分布不匹配的问题。
教师网络首先在未标注的数据集上进行预训练，以获取相关的结构信息，这些信息随后会指导学生分割网络的运行过程。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
在三维电子显微镜中，半监督神经元分割对于连接组学研究具有重要意义，因为它能够在减少对昂贵人工标注依赖的同时实现精确的神经元重建。然而，现有方法仍受限于少量标记数据集与大量未标记数据集之间的分布差异——标记数据无法充分反映真实的数据分布，从而导致基于这些数据训练出的模型生成质量较低的分割结果，进而影响整体性能。为解决这一问题，我们提出了一种基于相似性机制的半监督三维电子显微镜神经元分割方法（SimCP-NS）。该方法通过交换相似度最低的标记子体积与未标记子体积来丰富数据多样性，从而缓解分布不匹配的问题。首先在未标记数据集上预训练教师网络以获取结构信息，该网络随后用于指导学生网络的训练过程；在学生网络训练过程中，相似性复制机制会生成混合样本，并通过将教师网络生成的伪标签与真实亲和图融合来构建监督目标，这些目标是通过均方误差损失函数进行优化的。此外，该方法还整合了不变表示学习技术以提高其鲁棒性。大量实验结果表明，SimCP-NS在性能上显著优于现有的三维电子显微镜神经元分割方法。

**结果**：为了解决这一问题，我们提出了一种基于相似性机制的半监督三维电子显微镜神经元分割方法（SimCP-NS）。该方法通过交换相似度最低的标记子体积与未标记子体积来丰富数据多样性，从而缓解分布不匹配的问题。首先，我们在未标记数据集上预训练一个教师网络以捕获结构信息，该网络随后用于指导学生网络的训练过程。在学生网络训练过程中，相似性复制机制会生成混合样本，并通过将教师网络生成的伪标签与真实亲和图融合来构建监督目标，这些目标是通过均方误差损失函数进行优化的。此外，我们还整合了不变表示学习技术以提升该方法的鲁棒性。大量实验结果表明，SimCP-NS在性能上显著优于现有的三维电子显微镜神经元分割方法。  

**补充信息**：相关代码及辅助材料详见补充材料部分。

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Semi-supervised neuron segmentation in 3D electron microscopy (EM) is important for connectomics because it enables accurate neuron reconstruction while reducing dependence on costly manual annotations. However, existing approaches remain limited by the distribution mismatch between the small labeled dataset and the much larger unlabeled dataset, where the labeled data fails to adequately capture the true data distribution, leading models trained on them to generate low-quality segmentation masks and ultimately degrading overall performance.

RESULTS: To address this issue, we propose a similarity-based copy-paste for semi-supervised 3D EM neuron segmentation (SimCP-NS) method, which employs a similarity-based copy-paste strategy to exchange the least similar labeled and unlabeled sub-volumes, thereby enriching data diversity and mitigating distribution mismatch. A teacher network is first pre-trained on unlabeled volumes to capture structural priors, which subsequently guides the student segmentation network. During student training, the similarity-based copy-paste mechanism generates hybrid samples and constructs supervision targets by fusing teacher-generated pseudo-labels with ground-truth affinity maps, optimized via mean squared error loss. Invariant representation learning is further integrated to enhance robustness of the proposed method. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of SimCP-NS over existing 3D EM neuron segmentation methods.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Codes and other supporting materials are provided in the Supplementary Material.

all_papers.title: Quantitative imaging of dynamic processes in intestinal organoids
all_papers.summary: We present a Protocol for long-term imaging of intestinal organoids, in combination with OrganoidTracker software, that enables both single-cell tracking analysis for use in dynamic cell type inference and fluorescence intensity measurements
all_papers.llm_title_zh: 肠道类器官动态过程的定量成像研究
all_papers.llm_title_bilingual: 肠道类器官动态过程的定量成像研究 / Quantitative imaging of dynamic processes in intestinal organoids
all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 我们提出了一种用于长期观察肠道类器官的实验方案。该方案结合了 OrganoidTracker 软件，能够实现单细胞追踪分析，从而有助于动态推断细胞类型并测量荧光强度。
